verdicts.claim: inverse reformulation g(k)=max{n: f(n)<=k} and f(n)/log n -> infinity <=> g(k)^{1/k} -> 1
verdicts.note: both directions re-proved; the equivalence is conditional on f(n) -> infinity, i.e. on Erdos-Turan, which the scout does not flag. 'g finite precisely because f >> log n' overstates: f -> infinity suffices.

verdicts.claim: f(n-1) <= f_0(n) <= f(n); positivity mismatch harmless for the limit
verdicts.note: proof correct step by step; small table reproduced independently over [0,30]/[1,30]: f=0,1,2,2,3 and f_0=0,0,2,2,3
verdicts.sharpening: f(1)=0, f(2)=1, f(3)=2, f(4)=2 are exact and proved. f(5)=3 is NOT proved: f(5)>=3 is equivalent to g(2)<=4, which is open.

verdicts.claim: a supermultiplicative composition law g(k1+k2) >= g(k1)g(k2) refutes the conjecture
verdicts.note: Fekete is unnecessary; g(k) >= g(1)^k = 2^k follows by direct induction.
verdicts.strengthening: Erdos-Turan gives g(k) <= 3*2^(k-1) - 1, so such a law would pin g(k) into [2^k, 1.5*2^k], determining the growth constant to within 3/2. The 1934 bound is exactly sharp at k=1 (g(1)=2).
verdicts.finite_refutation_target: g(3) <= 7 would refute supermultiplicativity outright; Erdos-Turan gives g(3) <= 11 and search gives g(3) >= 5.

verdicts.claim: g_N(k) = 2,4,5,6,8,10,11 for k=1..7 with S = first k primes
corrections: 'every optimal witness lives below 50' is an artifact of search order: the witness set is closed under multiplication by S-units and under division by gcd, so optima come in infinite scaling orbits with a unique gcd-1 representative. Our largest-first search returned 162*{1,5,7,11} at k=2.

the table is never compared against the known 1934 construction A={1..m}, which gives g(k) >= (p_k+1)/2 ~ (1/2) k log k (e.g. g(7) >= 9). Any g_N table should be reported as max(g_N(k), ceil((p_k+1)/2)).

verdicts.claim: loose thread: |A| <= p-1 when p not in S, by pigeonhole on r <-> -r
verdicts.why: the constraint only forbids classes r and -r both occupied, and class 0 twice. A class r with 2r != 0 mod p may be occupied arbitrarily often. p=2 is the unique prime where the argument works, because Z/2 is the only Z/p in which every class is self-annihilating.
verdicts.unbounded_family: A = {1,4,7,...,3m-2} has all off-diagonal sums == 2 mod 3, so 3 divides no sum, for every m

verdicts.claim: the problem has no progress beyond 1934
verdicts.true_part: erdosproblems.com/126 (accessed 2026-08-24) records the problem as open, $250, with Erdos-Turan 1934 giving log n << f(n) << n/log n and the upper bound trivial from A={1..n}; the order of magnitude is unimproved and Furedi-Gyarmati (Feb 2026) still quote 3*2^(k-1)
missing_literature: Gyory, Stewart, Tijdeman 1986: two-set generalisation, omega(prod_{a in A, b in B}(a+b)) >= c log|A| with c effectively computable
Erdos, Stewart, Tijdeman 1988: near-optimality, sets with |A|=k, |B|=2 and omega < (1/8+eps)(log|A|)^2/log log|A|
Furedi, Gyarmati, arXiv:2602.07545 (Feb 2026), submitted to Acta Arithmetica: Erdos-Turan over Eulerian integers and binary forms
verdicts.strategic_note: the 1988 result says the two-set analogue can be as small as (log n)^2 / log log n, which is the shape f would have if the conjecture is true. Neither hunt document cites any paper.

new_route.name: explicit reduction to the three-term S-unit equation
new_route.proposition: if A={a,b,c,d} are distinct positive integers with all six off-diagonal sums S-smooth, then X+Y-Z=1 has a nondegenerate solution in positive S-units (take u=a+b, v=c+d, w=a+c, x=b+d; u+v=w+x; divide by u)
new_route.what_it_would_need: a solution count of the form exp(o(s)) for s=|S|; current bounds (Evertse; Evertse-Schlickewei-Schmidt) are exponential in s and reproduce 1934
new_route.not_obstructed: the known lower bound exp(c sqrt(s)/log s) (Erdos-Stewart-Tijdeman 1988) is itself exp(o(s)), so it does not forbid the needed upper bound
new_route.load_bearing_gap: the step from binom(n,4) unit-equation instances to binom(n,4) DISTINCT solutions is not proved here

unsettled: g(2): 4 or 5. Erdos-Turan gives <=5, search gives >=4.
g(3) <= 7, which would retire the composition programme.
